title: Consumer compatibility
summary: Ordinary producer PR updates and main pushes run producer CI without automatically dispatching hosted consumer integration. Releases create and await unconditional exact product/consumer commit-pair proof before tag publication, reusing only matching evidence under the existing durable release authority. Retries and simultaneous stage/prod callers join one immutable-pair run; a changed consumer or producer commit requires its own proof. Missing, failed, cancelled, timed-out or mismatched proof refuses publication with recovery. Explicit diagnostics dispatch the existing Platform pin-check workflow with product_ref and an exact consumer commit, without advisory caching. Each release accepts about nine minutes before tagging; stage and prod share one proof per pair within the bridge 120-minute limit, and Platform checks run in parallel. Reduced Actions consumption accepts later discovery of integration failures; producer review, QA and merge checks remain intact. Mandatory release verification remains, so the former combined workflow cost pool is not a promised saving. Consumer code changes require a linked companion; verification alone needs none. Release failure attribution names the producer commit interval and item references without inventing a culprit.
recipes: yoke github-actions dispatch-receipt get REQUEST-ID --project P --json
verification: Source tests verify release failure attribution from real Git history, candidate-tag exclusion, bootstrap ancestry and named unavailable-history recovery. Existing bridge tests require exact-pair proof before tagging. Live release proof remains unclaimed.
